spec.title: Testing: the pyramid, the testkit, replay fixtures, the contract test and CI

item.title: The contract test against the real scripts
The test plan every build ticket carries

spec.purpose: Every domain proves itself with fakes in seconds, the whole scheduler proves itself against golden replays of the bash belt's cases, the executor proves itself against the real scripts, and CI runs all of it; nothing runs on the host.

section.title: What the testing domain decides
section.text: In: the bash belt's test cases as the oracle, the routes table, the real scripts. Out: the testkit package, the replay fixtures, the test images, the make targets, the CI stage.
Tests run in isolation, in containers; the architect writes the plan into the ticket before the work starts; templates are reused, not rewritten.

section.title: The pyramid
section.text: Unit: pure functions with values in and out, the fakes of the testkit for the edges; every domain's cases in its spec are this level.
Package integration: the file store, the ledger and the latches on a temporary directory; the executor on a real unix socket with stub scripts on the path.
Replay: the engine over the golden fixtures with the fake executor, plans and jobs compared with the expected files.
Contract: the real scripts in the test image, every verb once, every record the scheduler emits validated by the writer's own check.
End to end: the scratch herdr session with a stub agent, the acceptance of the cut-over domain.

section.title: The testkit
section.text: FakeExecutor: answers each Run from a script keyed by verb and argument pattern (exit code, tails, delay or timeout); records every call in order; can fail Health on demand. Cases assert on its call log, as the bash cases do on the stub's.
World: a temporary directory with roots, a state directory, the tables copied from the repository and a configuration rendered with the variables pointing into it.
Clock: a settable time; Advance moves it so deadlines, windows and backoff are tested without waiting.

Record builder: writes record files in the writer's exact layout and shape for a kind, code, seat, ticket and attempt, one second apart when order matters; the contract test proves the builder against the writer.
The testkit is written by the skeleton ticket with core, so every domain's tests compile from their first day; a fake a domain needs that is missing is a question, not an edit.

section.title: Replay fixtures
section.text: One directory per case under testdata replay: the records in order, a context file (escalation history, seat statuses), and an expected file with, per record id, the verdict, the row index and the jobs with verb, arguments and order.
Each fixture is derived from a bash belt case: the same records, the same expected calls, so the Go engine proves the belt's behaviour before it proves its own improvements.
A case may carry an expected improvement: where the belt wrote a 500 the expected file says held or retry; the parity report's improvement count reads the same marker.
Fixtures are synthetic: no real ticket id, seat name, person or path; the check config's forbidden patterns apply to them.

section.title: Coverage of the table
section.text: Every row of the routes table is the chosen row of at least one replay record, and every policies row is exercised by at least one case; the replay suite fails naming the row that has none.
Every verb in the table is sent by at least one replay case and run by the contract test.

section.title: The contract test against the real scripts
section.text: For every record kind the scheduler emits, the arguments it would pass are run through the real writer in the test image and the result validated by the writer's check; a schema change in the log fails this test before it fails the line.
The seat and queue scripts run with their usage flags against the real files, so a changed flag or exit class is caught; their real actions are stubbed as the bash cases stub them.
The bash runner is run once in the test image over a fixture log and its ledger compared word for word with the Go ledger over the same log.

section.title: Images
section.text: The test image: the pinned Go image plus bash, jq and shellcheck, so Go tests, the contract test and the host wrappers' tests run in one container with the repository mounted read-only and the network off.
The module cache is a named volume filled once with the network on; every test run after that is offline.

section.title: CI
section.text: A stage runs the module's test target when the scheduler directory changes, in the test image on the build agents, which are a different architecture: the Go image is multi-architecture and the tests are architecture-neutral.
The repository lint already validates the configuration files; the lint ticket adds the scheduler specs' check script to it.

section.title: The test plan every build ticket carries
section.text: Each build ticket's test plan follows the test plan template: scope under test, cases with intent, command and expected, isolation naming the test image by digest, and what CI covers instead. The cases are the ones its domain spec lists.
The tester runs exactly those cases through the module's test target in the test image and nothing else.

section.title: Cases the build ticket proves

case.expected: exit 0: the fake executor answers by pattern, logs calls in order, injects a timeout; the clock advances; the builder writes a record the writer's check accepts
exit 0: every fixture's expected file equals the engine's plans and the fake executor's calls
exit 0: every routes row index appears as a chosen row in some fixture; a row with none fails naming it
exit 0: every emitted record kind passes the writer's check; every verb runs against the real scripts' usage
